text:
Rafael Mendes: retro thread for today’s staging game day (controlled regional impairment). drop what worked / what was noisy / changes before we do the low-risk prod slice.

incident-bot: Reminder: add action items to Linear and link in the game day plan. Use :white_check_mark: when filed.

Miles Thornton: overall: trigger engine + orchestrator wiring held up. state machine transitions were sane (no loops) and we could force a rollback cleanly.

Miles Thornton: biggest win: progressive failover % actually behaved the way we described (10% -> 25% -> 50%). rollback path didn’t require manual policy edits (thank you 🙏).

Mina Haddad: +1. routing policy store updates were consistent. BUT the eval logs were hard to follow in real time. we need a single “why did we transition?” line w/ evaluated signals + window + thresholds.

Allison Grant: agree. the audit entries are there but too verbose and spread across services. ideally one canonical “decision record” per transition that links out to raw metrics.

Aisha Bello: what worked on alerting: burn-rate alert didn’t page us unnecessarily, it only fired when we were actually sustaining elevated errors.

Aisha Bello: what was noisy: tail latency (p99) alert was flapping when we toggled load shedding. it’s measuring the *new* shed behavior + retries, not true backend latency.

Sergio Costa: yep. dashboard made it look like we were “worse” after mitigation because p99 moved around as we shed. we should chart: admitted latency vs end-to-end latency vs shed rate.

Tomáš Novák: runbook usability notes:
- “monitor-only” vs “active” mode isn’t obvious enough when you’re stressed.
- the stop conditions checklist is solid, but we need a short version at the top (TL;DR) before the long explanation.
- rollback section needs an explicit “what to check after rollback” (queue drain, error budget burn returns to baseline, model variant not stuck).

Connor O'Brien: release/chg mgmt note: we need a crisp list of required sign-offs for enabling “active” in prod. today it was too ad hoc in the moment.

Rafael Mendes: please propose (names/roles) + add to rollout plan doc.

Benji Okafor: safe-to-failover checks: capacity gate blocked the 25% step once (good!) but the reason was confusing. we were looking at GPU headroom from Fleet in 2 different places w/ different aggregation windows.

Harish Reddy: yeah, the “available tokens/sec” metric is lagging by ~2m. during game day it went red even though the pool was fine. we need to pick an authoritative metric + publish the contract.

Miles Thornton: action: tighten safe-to-failover contract:
- authoritative headroom signal (one)
- required freshness / max staleness
- if stale => treat as UNKNOWN, not FAIL, and don’t advance steps (but also don’t auto-rollback?)

Aisha Bello: for stale/UNKNOWN, i’d prefer: block advancing, but don’t auto-rollback unless error budget burn is high. otherwise we create failure loops on telemetry issues.

Mina Haddad: +1. also, dependency health checks were too sensitive. the synthetic probe from eu-west to us-east had a brief packet loss blip and we treated it like the whole target region is unhealthy.

Allison Grant: the probe should be multi-vantage and thresholded (N of M failing). right now it’s “any failing => unhealthy”. that’s basically guaranteed false positives.

Sergio Costa: can we also label probes with “blast radius relevance”? e.g. an inter-region probe failing doesn’t necessarily mean customer traffic is broken if ingress is fine.

Miles Thornton: we should split: ingress health, intra-region health, and cross-region path health. cross-region should gate failover steps only if we’re actually moving traffic that requires cross-region dependencies.

Ethan Park: control plane note: orchestrator API was hammered a bit by observers refreshing. we should add caching to the status endpoint and a rate limit (or at least a “watch” stream).

Tomáš Novák: comms: we used #incidents-style cadence even though it was a game day. that was good. BUT we need a comms template for “paused/holding at 10% canary due to guardrail” so people don’t assume we’re stuck.

Rafael Mendes: what surprised folks?

Aisha Bello: the load shedding policy interacted with retries. some clients retried aggressively and we saw request amplification. if we do this in prod we need either client guidance or stricter server-side retry headers.

Mina Haddad: +1. also the fallback model variant selection kicked in for some routes when latency was high, but it wasn’t obvious in the dashboard. customers might interpret this as “model changed”. we need visibility + maybe tier gating.

Sergio Costa: dashboard action: add panels:
- % traffic on fallback variant (by route + tier)
- shed rate by route
- failover step (% shifted)
- decision log link

Allison Grant: and annotate state transitions on all charts (vertical markers). right now you have to eyeball timestamps.

Connor O'Brien: prod-readiness gating ask: before we do low-risk slice, I want:
1) hold-down timer confirmed + tested (no flappy oscillations)
2) one-click manual override (pause + rollback)
3) clear rollback SLO verification checklist
4) alert routing confirmed (who gets paged vs who gets FYI)

Miles Thornton: hold-down timer test: we didn’t simulate recovery oscillation enough. today the region “recovered” cleanly. we should add a scenario where error rate dips below threshold briefly then spikes.

Rafael Mendes: can someone file a follow-up scenario in the test matrix? :point_right:

Tomáš Novák: i’ll file. :white_check_mark: (will link)

Benji Okafor: another noisy thing: logs. we had three different correlation IDs (edge, routing, orchestrator). can we standardize so the audit entry includes the request sample ID(s) that drove the decision?

Ethan Park: yes. we can propagate one “failover_evaluation_id” per evaluation window and attach it everywhere.

Aisha Bello: +1. also for paging, can we avoid paging on “entered DEGRADED” when it’s a game day? we should have a test mode that downgrades pages to Slack notifications.

Connor O'Brien: careful there — in prod we want the page. for tests, we can use an allowlist of routes/tiers + a “game_day” flag that changes routing of alerts.

Rafael Mendes: summary / decisions:
- adjust probe health semantics (N/M + categorize cross-region)
- pick authoritative capacity signal + staleness policy
- improve decision/audit log readability (one canonical per transition)
- dashboards: admitted vs end-to-end latency, shed %, fallback %, state markers
- runbook TL;DR + clearer mode indicator + post-rollback checks
- add oscillation scenario to staging test matrix before prod

Rafael Mendes: action items — please reply with Linear ticket IDs when created.

Tomáš Novák: filed oscillation scenario + runbook edits as ENG-2850 follow-ups (commented). :white_check_mark:

Sergio Costa: I’ll file dashboard updates + annotations, will post link in a sec.

Harish Reddy: I’ll draft the capacity metric contract + staleness rules w/ Benji. will loop in Fleet.

Miles Thornton: I’ll take the canonical decision record / evaluation_id propagation.

Mina Haddad: I’ll take probe semantics + routing implications (split health types). will coordinate w/ Infra.

Rafael Mendes: thanks all. keep thread going as you remember more. next checkpoint tomorrow to confirm what blocks prod low-risk slice.
